- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., 73.08 → 74.81 in Example 1), then undercorrects later.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or lagged response to recent high prices.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, which show more volatility and sharper transitions.
- Model fails to capture the “late surge” in price (e.g., 75.54–79.16 in Example 1) — likely underestimates demand or policy shocks.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after spikes.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting calibration issue with upward momentum or volatility clustering.
